subject: Request for custom SLA addendum, evidence & order-form language
messages:
From: Erin Collins <erin.collins@astramed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom SLA addendum for enterprise MSA/SOW attachments & order form language

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is impressed with Redwood's routing and fallback model variants. Procurement & legal at AstraMed are now starting the contract pass and we have a couple of asks before we can sign the MSA + order form. High level: we need a short SLA addendum (exhibit) and matching order-form language that capture an availability / latency exception we require for our clinical production workloads.

What we need from Redwood:
- A draft SLA exhibit (DocuSign-ready) that reflects the following carve-outs: 99.95% uptime for production endpoints (global), with an explicit maintenance window allowance and regional fallback behavior.
- Latency commitment: p95 < 200ms for generation requests at our expected QPS profile; we understand this may require dedicated capacity or a specific instance type — please call out options and pricing delta.
- A clear credits schedule for availability breaches and an operational escalation path (who we call at 10/30/60 minutes).
- Evidence packet: 30 / 90 day historical uptime & latency reports, KB on maintenance windows, and an ops runbook for incidents impacting availability.

I'm attaching our redlines to the MSA and a short spreadsheet with expected traffic patterns. Timeline: procurement would like a draft exhibit and order-form text by Friday, Aug 4 so legal can slot it into the signature packet.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet the p95 latency target in us-west region for ~120 rps sustained, and what the order-form language would look like for a dedicated pool + burst allowance? Also include any monitoring/tracing evidence we can push to our SREs.

Thanks — Erin
Erin Collins
Head of Procurement, AstraMed Solutions
erin.collins@astramed.com
+1 (415) 555-0119

Attachments: AstraMed_SLA_redlines_20280731.pdf (pdf), MSA_v3-AstraMed-redline.docx (docx), redline_notes.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Aug 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum for enterprise MSA/SOW attachments & order form language

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines.

Short answer: yes, we can support a 99.95% availability exhibit and we can produce p95 latency evidence for us-west at the scales you described, but hitting 200ms p95 reliably at 120 rps will typically require either a dedicated capacity pool or a higher-concurrency plan (we'll detail pricing). Below is a proposed implementation path and deliverables we can get to you by Aug 4.

Proposed path (timeline to Aug 4):
1) Legal/Order-form draft (Soojin/Kimberly) — provide DocuSign-ready SLA exhibit language and order-form clause for dedicated pool + burst.
2) Evidence pack (Ben/Operations) — 30/90-day availability summary, latency p50/p95/p99 histograms for our comparable deployments in us-west, incident RTO/RPO examples, and maintenance schedule.
3) Ops runbook & escalation — named contacts, 10/30/60 minute paging path, and regional failover behavior.
4) Pricing delta — line item for dedicated pool and optional burst credits, plus how credits are calculated on breaches.

What we'll deliver by Friday: draft SLA exhibit (PDF), order-form language snippet (to insert into the order), and a short evidence bundle. If AstraMed wants, we can also prepare a short appendix that describes how prefix-caching and KV cache retention affects cold-start latency for long-context workflows.

Questions for you (to finalize wording):
- Confirm target region(s) for the exhibit (you mentioned us-west; do you also want eu-west?)
- Confirm desired recovery window tolerance for planned maintenance (we usually allow a 4-hour monthly maintenance window in the exhibit unless we negotiate otherwise).
- Are you expecting a full dedicated pool locked for AstraMed, or would a burst-enabled shared pool with guaranteed throughput suffice?

Relationals: I'll drop a HubSpot note and create a DocuSign envelope once Kimberly signs off on order-form language.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0274

Attachments: SLA_exhibit_template_v2.pdf (draft)

Subject: Fwd: Request: custom SLA addendum for enterprise MSA/SOW attachments & order form language

Team — forwarding AstraMed's redlines and ask. Timeline is tight (they want draft exhibits by Aug 4). Can we coordinate quickly? Below are specific action items; I'm happy to sync for 20 minutes this afternoon.

Ben: please assemble an evidence pack with the following items (30 / 90 day where possible):
- Availability summary (daily uptime %) for services with similar inference profiles (us-west)
- Latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) for typical generation requests, plus p95 under sustained 120 rps load
- List of scheduled maintenance windows in the last 90 days and description of our maintenance notification process
- Ops runbook excerpt that shows escalation path and 10/30/60 minute routing (names/roles only)

Kimberly: please draft the order-form snippet and SLA exhibit language that we can hand to legal and AstraMed. Key points:
- Exhibit should state 99.95% uptime, allowed monthly maintenance window, regional fallback behavior, and a credits schedule for breaches.
- Include an option block for dedicated pool pricing (flat monthly commit) vs. burst-enabled shared pool (usage-based uplift + priority routing).
- Call out monitoring artifacts we will provide (CSV/JSON histograms + Grafana snapshot link) and deliverable timelines.

Attachments included in original: AstraMed_SLA_redlines_20280731.pdf, MSA_v3-AstraMed-redline.docx, redline_notes.xlsx (see HubSpot link).

I'll create a HubSpot task and a DocuSign envelope once we have the exhibit + order snippet ready. Please reply with ETA — if you can get a first draft by end of day today that would be ideal.

Thanks — Soojin
